memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make all its utensils of bronze — its pots to remove the ashes, and its shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. Make a grating for it, a bronze network, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the network." - Exodus 27:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the metal. Inside the tabernacle, everything was gold — the ark, the table, the lampstand. But out at the altar, everything was bronze: the utensils, the grating, the rings. Bronze was the tougher metal, the one that could withstand constant heat without being destroyed. Where fire burned continually, God specified a material that could bear it.

There is wisdom in that choice. God matches the material to the task. He did not put delicate gold where the flames were; He put bronze, made to endure. And He does something similar with His people. The person facing a season of fire is not left with equipment unsuited to it. God provides what the situation actually requires.

Paul writes that God is faithful, and will not let us be tested beyond what we can bear, but will provide a way through (1 Cor 10:13). This is not a promise that fire will not come — the altar always had fire. It is a promise that God equips us for what He allows. If you are in a burning season right now, do not assume you have been given the wrong materials for it. The God who chose bronze for the altar knows exactly what your position requires, and He supplies it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I facing a "fire" and assuming I am not equipped for it?
How has God provided what I actually needed in past difficult seasons?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know what each position requires and You supply it. When I face fire, help me trust that You have equipped me, and give me strength to endure well. Amen.
